_doc: OUTPUT CONTRACTS — what each scheduled job MUST persist. Committed manifest; the dead-man checks the commit DIFF against it, so a job that ran-but-persisted-nothing goes red instead of green. Created 2026-08-05 by the fail-loud hardening session after the judge-log instance (a run that succeeded, cost $4.00, and committed nothing).
_standard: S2-F3's receipt standard applied to OUTPUTS, not just firings: the proof that a job worked is the commit diff it produced, not that the workflow exited 0.
_enforcement: scripts/output_contracts.py -> check_output_contracts(); surfaced in results/weekly_monitor.json under scheduler_health.output_contracts and annotated ::error on the next monitor run.

contracts.note: judge_log is conditional: it only grows when the judge step logs rows (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Listed separately so a missing key reads as a WARN, not a contract breach. base_swing_forward.json is the forward/prereg_swing.md §4 comparator arm (all grades, WATCHED, never surfaced — it holds Grade-B names). Added 2026-08-08 and listed conditionally until the first successful persist, per the same rule as intraday-scan below; promote it to must_update once one run has written it, because from then on a week missing is a week of the §4 comparison permanently lost (§3 forbids backfilling reconstructed history).

must_update is EMPTY and must stay empty until the first successful persist. The whitelist that made `git add results/intraday_scan/` a silent no-op was only fixed 2026-08-05 (the fifth instance of the trap), so no historical commit can satisfy a hard contract. Promote to must_update once a scan has demonstrably landed. || PREFIX CORRECTED 2026-08-25. The workflow's commit subject changed to 'chore(scan): 16:30 IST post-close shadow scan' when the job moved from 14:30 to post-close, and this manifest was not changed with it. The checker matches on the SUBJECT, so it kept scoring the last 14:30-era commit (2026-08-10) and reported the job 15 days stale while it was in fact committing a scan every trading day — 15 consecutive days of RED from one stale string. That is the exact failure this module's docstring names: a false positive in an alarm is as damaging as a missed defect, because it is how alarms stop being read. tests/test_output_contracts.py now pins every commit_prefix to the workflow that emits it, so a rename cannot silently desynchronise them again.

S-F1, closed 2026-08-06: forward/prereg.md calls the 3-book wall 'the only certifier' and specifies a DAILY log, and until this workflow existed it had no scheduled producer at all. forward_wall_start.json is the wall's registered start — written once by the first run and never rewritten — so it is contracted alongside the log itself: without it a cold start would backfill recomputed history into the wall as forward evidence. The commit subject carries the Actions run id, which is the S2-F3 firing-evidence cross-check that S2-F4 (owner-authored cron commits) otherwise weakens. || DOWNGRADED TO CONDITIONAL 2026-08-08, with a date to restore it. nq/paper/wall_cron._assert_veto_arm_live now refuses to append any row whose session post-dates the veto arm's factor coverage — data/ff_india_factors.parquet ends 2026-06-29, before the wall's own 2026-07-02 start floor, and no cron rebuilds it. Before that guard the arm was silently inert and the wall would have written base==veto agreement it never measured into a hash-chained log. So the wall correctly produces nothing, and a hard contract would read that correctness as a daily breach. The veto arm's fate is a §7 demotion decision and §8 confines it to a quarterly review: 2026-10-01. RESTORE these three to must_update at that review, whichever way it goes — retire the arm and the wall logs two books, or extend the factors and it logs three.
